query: WITH recent AS (SELECT id FROM orders WHERE created_at > '2025-01-01') SELECT * FROM recent;
note: Star in the outer query of a CTE is still top-level

query: SELECT id FROM orders o WHERE EXISTS (SELECT * FROM users u WHERE u.id = o.user_id) LIMIT 10;
note: SELECT * inside EXISTS is a harmless idiom and not top-level

query: UPDATE orders SET status = 'archived' WHERE id IN (SELECT order_id FROM archive_queue);
note: UPDATE has a real WHERE clause

query: SELECT name FROM users WHERE created_at >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '7 days' LIMIT 10;
note: Function and arithmetic on the value side only; column stays index-friendly

query: SELECT id FROM users WHERE TRIM(name) = 'bob' LIMIT 5;
note: TRIM was not in the old regex function list; tests that the rule generalises

query: /* cleanup */ DROP TABLE IF EXISTS staging_orders;
note: Real DROP after a block comment must still fire

query: SELECT id FROM docs WHERE title LIKE 'report%' LIMIT 10;
note: Trailing wildcard can use a B-tree index

query: SELECT u.id, o.total FROM users u LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = u.id AND o.status = 'paid';
note: Filter in ON is the correct fix for the LEFT JOIN trap, not the trap itself

query: SELECT a.id FROM accounts a WHERE a.email = 'x@y.com' OR a.phone = '123' LIMIT 10;
note: Different columns, both qualified with the same alias

query: SELECT id FROM orders ORDER BY id LIMIT 10 OFFSET 20;
UPDATE users SET last_seen = NOW() -- WHERE id = 5
note: The only WHERE is commented out, so every row is updated

query: SELECT 'SELECT * FROM users' AS example FROM docs LIMIT 1;
note: SELECT * appears only inside a string literal

query: select * from orders o join users u on u.id = o.user_id where lower(u.email) = 'a@b.com' order by o.created_at desc
note: Lowercase, inner join, three issues at once
